item.title: ChatGPT Chrome Extension Gains Ability to Read and Act on Open Tabs
item.description:
ChatGPT Chrome Extension Gains Ability to Read and Act on Open Tabs

OpenAI has refreshed its ChatGPT Chrome extension, letting the assistant look at the tabs you already have open and use that context for a variety of tasks.

🔍 Overview

  • The previous ChatGPT Atlas browser is gone, but the Chrome extension now lets ChatGPT view your browser tabs when you tag Chrome in the web or desktop app.
  • OpenAI shared a demo video where a user asks ChatGPT to compare three open tabs that show different sofas.

🧩 How it Works

  • With the extension installed, ChatGPT can pull information from your open tabs or appear in a sidebar next to the page you’re viewing.
  • The sidebar provides “the full power of ChatGPT” and keeps your entire conversation history in Chat or Work without leaving the page.
  • ChatGPT Work can control Chrome tabs for actions such as sending messages, filling out forms, or downloading files, similar to Google’s Gemini‑powered “auto browse” feature.

⚙️ Key Features

  • Tab peeking – ChatGPT can see the titles and contents of the tabs you have open.
  • Cross‑tab comparison – It can compare items across multiple tabs (e.g., sofas, contractor services).
  • Data extraction – Pull vendor details, pricing, key features, and source links from open tabs into a comparison sheet.
  • Form assistance – Fill out registration or appointment forms that are open in Chrome.
  • Email drafting – Draft emails based on the tab that best fits a described need.
  • Calendar integration – Add appointments to work and personal calendars.
  • Tab control – Send messages, download files, and organize or group tabs directly from the AI.

📋 Sample Queries

Sample Query What ChatGPT Does
Use the details in this event brief to fill out the registration form, and stop before submitting. Extracts information from the brief, populates the open registration form, pauses before final submission.
Put the vendors in these tabs into my comparison sheet, with pricing, key features, and source links. Reads vendor data from open tabs and populates a spreadsheet with the requested fields.
Look at all the tabs I have open and compare the contractor services. Reviews each open tab, extracts service details, and generates a side‑by‑side comparison.
Then draft an email to the one that fits my home renovation. Crafts an email addressed to the selected contractor based on the comparison.
Fill out the form I have open in @chrome ahead of seeing my new dentist. Completes the dental appointment form using the information provided.
Also, can you add the appointment to my work and personal calendar. Creates calendar events in both work and personal calendars for the appointment.

🚀 Availability

  • The upgraded capabilities are available to anyone who installs the ChatGPT Chrome extension. No additional software is required beyond the extension itself.

#OpenAI #ChatGPT #ChromeExtension #AIProductivity

Source: ChatGPT can peek at your Chrome tabs now

item.title: Square launches Square Kiosk with conversational AI ordering interface
item.description:
Square launches Square Kiosk with conversational AI ordering interface

Square announced a new hardware product that blends a large touchscreen kiosk with a conversational AI assistant for ordering.

🔍 Overview

  • The device is called the Square Kiosk.
  • It is a big kiosk with a 21.5‑inch touchscreen and a pill‑shaped form factor.
  • An “agentic, conversational voice layer” lets customers talk to the AI as they would to staff.

🧩 How it works

  • Presence detection greets customers as they approach the kiosk.
  • While speaking with the AI agent, users can:
    • Ask questions about the menu.
    • Request modifications and substitutions.
    • Receive real‑time responses that fully understand the seller’s menu.
  • When ordering is complete, payment can be made via a contactless payment reader or a card slot.

⚙️ Key details

  • Screen size: 21.5 inches.
  • Form factor: Large pill shape.
  • AI capabilities: Real‑time listening, menu comprehension, natural‑language ordering.
  • Payment options: Contactless reader and card slot.

🚀 Availability

  • The Square Kiosk is available starting today.
  • Price: $1,999 per device for businesses with a Square Plus or Premium subscription.
  • Ongoing software fee: $99 per device per month.

#Square #AI #Kiosk #Payments #ConversationalAI

Source: Square’s new kiosk lets you talk to AI for help with your order

item.title: Short AI Use Reduces Focus and Persistence, New Study Shows
item.description:
Short AI Use Reduces Focus and Persistence, New Study Shows

A peer‑reviewed study presented this week at the Conference on Language Modeling found that just ten minutes of AI assistance can significantly impair people’s ability to stay focused and persist on difficult tasks.

🔍 Overview

  • The research was led by a multinational team that includes scholars from Carnegie Mellon University, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, the University of Oxford, UCLA, and a research fellow with the UC Berkeley Center for Human‑Compatible AI, Brian Christian.
  • The paper builds on earlier preliminary drafts that generated media coverage from WIRED, Psychology Today, and the New York Times.

⚙️ Study Design

  • Researchers ran three randomized controlled trials with a total of 1,222 online participants.
  • Experiment 1 (354 participants): one group solved 15 basic fraction problems alone, another group solved the same problems with ChatGPT open for assistance and answer requests.
  • Experiment 2 (667 participants): a larger replication of the fraction‑problem design.
  • Experiment 3 (201 participants): participants tackled an SAT‑style reading‑comprehension prompt under the same AI‑access vs. no‑AI conditions.

📊 Key Findings

  • In the first experiment, the AI‑access group started off more accurate than the no‑AI group.
  • After participants completed 12 problems, the AI tool was removed.
  • Immediate drop: the AI‑access group’s accuracy and persistence fell sharply as soon as ChatGPT was taken away.
  • In the larger second experiment, AI users either gave wrong answers or gave up entirely when assistance was withdrawn, while the no‑AI group continued working and ended with higher success.
  • The third experiment echoed the same pattern: removal of the AI tool led to reduced persistence and accuracy on the reading task.
  • The authors conclude that short‑term reliance on AI erodes “cognitive fitness” by eliminating the “productive struggle” that helps people develop research strengths and passions.

💡 Why It Matters

  • Overreliance on AI for rapid answers can make slower, effortful problem‑solving feel inefficient.
  • Frontier AI companies acknowledge that offloading tasks to chatbots can lower baseline understanding and mastery of subjects.
  • Christian warns that in research and academia, excessive AI assistance could jeopardize core scientific habits: staying close to data, immersing in material, and collaborating in teams.
  • He suggests AI responses could default to a more instructive, tutor‑like style rather than providing instant answers.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Team Affiliations

Institution Role

Massachusetts Institute of Technology Scholar
University of Oxford Scholar
UCLA Scholar
UC Berkeley Center for Human‑Compatible AI Research Fellow (Brian Christian)

item.title: Synthetic AI Voices Gain Human‑Like Disfluencies to Preserve Communication Nuance
item.description:
Synthetic AI Voices Gain Human‑Like Disfluencies to Preserve Communication Nuance

A recent article by Associate Professor Celeste Rodriguez Louro, Director of the Language Lab at The University of Western Australia, published in The Conversation on 8 October 2026, describes her experience listening to what she called “(literally) breathless AI voices for audiobooks.”

🔎 Overview

  • Communication does not begin and end with the speaker; words encounter a listener’s memories, expectations, assumptions, other languages, and even their current mood.
  • Even imperfections in speech—hesitations, repetitions, false starts—carry information. Linguists label these as “disfluencies.”
  • A synthetic voice that removes all disfluency can be grammatically correct and acoustically flawless, yet feel impoverished to the listener because it offers less communicative cues.

🗣️ Why Disfluencies Matter

  • Human language is more than a catalogue of words and pronunciations; it is a “living, breathing soup of memory and imagination” (as described by author Arundhati Roy).
  • Human communication is not a clean transfer of information; listeners interpret voices through social judgments, personality cues, and identity perceptions (research by Berkeley linguist Nicole Holliday).
  • Retaining identifiable, human‑like characteristics in synthetic speech can signal to listeners that they are interacting with a machine, which itself can have value.

🤖 Development Trends

  • Many technology companies are already adding conversational markers and disfluencies to synthetic voices to make them feel less mechanistic.
  • As robotics and human‑machine interaction become routine, synthetic voices may develop more convincing rhythm and prosody, recognising when a listener needs clarification, when a joke requires a pause, or when uncertainty should be expressed.
  • Conversely, the mechanistic “breathless” style—perfectly structured answers with no hesitation—could become a linguistic signature or watermark for generative AI models.
  • Researchers observed that autonomous AI agents, in September 2026 experiments, created unusual vocabulary, metaphors, and coded expressions that were difficult for humans to interpret, likening the emergence to innovative language in human communities.

📚 Implications for Language Representation

  • Synthetic systems can generate, consume, and interact with language at a scale and speed beyond human capability.
  • If synthetic voices retain recognizable traits, listeners can treat them as a distinct register rather than a flaw.
  • The central question shifts from “Does AI sound human?” to “Whose human language does the model represent, and what happens to voices of minoritised groups that fall outside the training data?”

Key take‑aways

  • Disfluencies are communicative resources, not errors.
  • Adding them to AI voices improves listener experience and social perception.
  • The emerging “synthetic register” may become a purposeful feature, not merely a shortcoming.
  • Ongoing research highlights the ethical dimension of which human languages and voices are embodied in AI models.

#AIvoices #Disfluency #HumanAIInteraction #Linguistics

Source: What happens to language when machines start talking back?

item.title: Keystroke Analysis Detects LLM‑Assisted Vietnamese Writing
item.description:
Keystroke Analysis Detects LLM‑Assisted Vietnamese Writing

A new study submitted on 6 Oct 2026 examines how keystroke dynamics can reveal when large language models (LLMs) assist Vietnamese text production, even when users try to hide their involvement.

🔍 Overview

  • Focuses on the robustness of keystroke‑based detection of LLM‑assisted writing.
  • Introduces a Vietnamese keystroke dataset covering multiple realistic writing modes.
  • Defines a behaviorally grounded threat model where users deliberately alter typing patterns.

🗂️ Dataset

  • Bona fide composition – natural, unaided Vietnamese typing.
  • Transcription – copying text verbatim.
  • Paraphrasing – re‑expressing content while preserving meaning.

⚙️ Threat Model

  • Users create behaviorally manipulated variants of the keystroke data to evade detection.
  • These manipulated samples are used to test the limits of keystroke‑based classifiers.

🤖 Models Evaluated

Model Representation Type
Temporal features Feature‑based
Rhythmic features Feature‑based
1D‑CNN Sequential
TypeNet Sequential
  • Evaluations are performed under user‑independent and context‑independent settings.

📊 Findings

  • Sequential models (1D‑CNN, TypeNet) outperform feature‑based approaches in most scenarios.
  • Keystroke signals contain discriminative information about the writing process.
  • Transcription is reliably identified.
  • Paraphrasing and adversarially manipulated samples are often misclassified as genuine when not explicitly modeled.
  • Applying adversarial training with behaviorally manipulated data markedly improves separability and robustness.

💡 Implications

  • Success of keystroke‑based detection hinges on exposure to a diverse range of writing behaviors.
  • Strong performance in limited conditions does not automatically generalize to realistic or adversarial environments without targeted modeling.

🚀 Community Context

  • The paper is hosted on arXiv, which collaborates with arXivLabs, a framework for developing and sharing new arXiv features while upholding openness, community, excellence, and user‑data privacy.

#keystrokes #LLMDetection #Vietnamese #AdversarialAI

Source: Detecting LLM-Assisted Vietnamese Writing via Keystrokes under Behavioral Manipulation
